chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The fasting one, when he fears for his eyes from the conjunctivitis (eye infection), breaks [his fast].
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking fast due to eye infection in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the principle of *darar* (harm) within the jurisprudence of fasting. It specifically highlights that fear of worsening a specific ailment, such as conjunctivitis (*al-ramad*), constitutes a valid medical excuse for breaking the fast, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving health as a primary objective of Shariah.
